## Resolution: Release 2 scope

Decided in a grilling session on 2026-11-10. Later tickets build against this list.

**In Release 2**

- **Themes:** generated when a Round closes, only for Rounds that meet the minimum group size. The Lead sees themes and keeps the redacted raw comments (as in R1); members see themes, never raw comments (SPEC §10 question 1 default). Rules in #88.
- **Redaction stays rule-based** (ADR 0009). No AI redaction: only already-redacted text ever leaves Cloudflare.
- **AI is opt-in per Organization:** an Organization admin turns "AI themes" on; off by default; while on, members are told in the answer flow. Provider decided in #87 (ADR 0015).
- **Discussion guide:** a short agenda for the Lead's team conversation: biggest change, lowest Dimension, open Actions by rules, plus AI-written prompts from themes when AI is on. Lead only. Details in #92.
- **Team health overview:** one Team's Dimensions across all its Rounds with Action markers (committed and done). Lead and members. No cross-Team view (R3 roll-ups). Details in #91.
- **Delayed sharing:** after close, the Lead reviews before members see Results; Results are shared when the Lead clicks "Share with the team" or automatically after 3 days. No indefinite withholding. Uses the existing Ready → Shared states. Details in #89.
- **Member's private history page:** which Rounds the member took part in (from Participation records), and their own past answers only from their own browser (stored with the Edit key). No server-side link (ADR 0005 unchanged); a new device shows no past answers and says so. Details in #90.
- **German:** app, answer page, and emails; language per Person, defaulting to the browser, then the Organization. Translations drafted by Claude, reviewed by the product owner. Details in #93.
- **First real Round:** the product owner's team starts weekly Rounds early in R2, once the #94 checklist passes, before R2 features land, so real comments inform themes and the guide.

**Not in Release 2:** every R1 deferral (eNPS, multiple choice, short text, the other Templates, shared-link Distribution, other cadences, one-off surveys, attributed and confidential modes, member-proposed Actions), unless the first real Round shows a need.

# OpenRouter with `meta/muse-ember` for comment processing

Research for issue #87 (map #85). Researched 2026-11-10 against openrouter.ai (docs, live APIs, model page, terms, DPA), Meta's Model API terms as linked from OpenRouter, and developers.cloudflare.com. No OpenRouter account or API key was used, so nothing below was confirmed by a real request.

**Why it matters.** The product owner chose OpenRouter with `meta/muse-ember` for the Release 2 AI pass over comments, replacing SPEC §10 question 4's default (Workers AI through AI Gateway, prompt logging off). ADR 0009 says raw comment text is never sent to a model, so only the already-redacted text can be sent. SPEC §7 makes the privacy rules release blockers. The ADR that follows this note has to record the provider, the request settings that enforce no retention, what is sent, and what members are told.

## TL;DR

1. **No zero data retention is possible.** `meta/muse-ember` has exactly one endpoint, served by Meta itself. OpenRouter lists it as `retainsPrompts: true`, `retentionDays: 30`, `training: false`, `is_zdr: false`. It is not in `/api/v1/endpoints/zdr`. With `provider.zdr: true`, or with ZDR enforced on the account or a guardrail, the model has no eligible endpoint and the request fails. No request body can make this model retention-free.
2. **US, not EU.** The model page says "Not currently available through EU in-region routing". The model is missing from both the EU and the US regional model lists. Meta's headquarters is listed as US. OpenRouter publishes no data centre location for Meta (`datacenters: null`, `provider_region: null`).
3. **JSON schema: yes.** The endpoint lists `response_format` and `structured_outputs`. Use `response_format: { type: "json_schema", json_schema: { strict: true, ... } }` on Chat Completions.
4. **Context length is 1,048,576 tokens.** The maximum completion is 943,718 tokens. Reasoning is mandatory (`effort: "none"` is rejected), and the default effort is `max`.
5. **Cost per Round: about $0.001 to $0.003.** Input costs $0.10 per million tokens and output $0.50 per million. One theming call over 20 comments of 300 characters is about 2,500 input and 1,500 to 4,500 output tokens, most of it reasoning. Reasoning tokens are billed as output, so set `reasoning.effort` low and cap `max_tokens`.
6. **A DPA exists and is part of OpenRouter's terms.** It includes Module 2 SCCs and an optional EU-only addendum (Exhibit A). The DPA does not stop Meta keeping prompts: OpenRouter's ZDR promise covers OpenRouter itself, and the provider's own terms govern the provider.
7. **Meta's terms leave a training gap.** Meta's terms split models into "Standard" models (no training) and "Contributor" models (Meta trains on content). Muse Ember was added to OpenRouter on 2026-11-09 and is not on Meta's designation list, which was last updated 2026-10-12. OpenRouter says `training: false`. Meta's own page is silent.
8. **Calling it from a Worker or Durable Object is simple.** Use `fetch` to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions` with the key from a Worker secret, an `AbortSignal.timeout`, and retries on 408/429/502/503 that honour `Retry-After`. Waiting on `fetch` does not count as CPU time.

## 1. The model and its single endpoint

Sources: <https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models/meta/muse-ember/endpoints>, the `meta/muse-ember` entry in <https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models>, and the data embedded in <https://openrouter.ai/meta/muse-ember>. All three were read on 2026-11-10.

| Field | Value |
| - | - |
| Canonical slug | `meta/muse-ember-20261109` (created 2026-11-09) |
| Endpoints | **One**: "Meta \| meta/muse-ember-20261109", provider slug `meta`, upstream `https://api.meta.ai/v1` |
| Context length | 1,048,576 tokens. `max_completion_tokens` 943,718 |
| Input modalities | text, image, video, file, audio. Output: text |
| Pricing | prompt $0.0000001/token ($0.10/M), completion $0.0000005/token ($0.50/M), cache read $0.004/M, cache write $0.125/M, web search $0.0025 |
| Supported parameters | `reasoning`, `include_reasoning`, `reasoning_effort`, `max_tokens`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `repetition_penalty`, `tools`, `tool_choice` (only `auto`), `response_format`, `structured_outputs` |
| Reasoning | `mandatory: true`, `default_effort: "max"`, efforts `max`, `xhigh`, `high`, `medium`, `low`, `minimal` |
| Moderation | `is_moderated: true`, `moderationRequired: true` |
| Implicit caching | `supports_implicit_caching: false` |
| Quantization | `unknown` |
| Uptime | 100% over 5 min, 30 min and 1 day |

**Latency** (model page, 30-minute window, about 27,500 requests): p50 1.8 s, p75 2.5 s, p90 3.4 s, p95 4.1 s, p99 5.9 s. Throughput p50 157 tokens/s, p99 18 tokens/s. The page labels this metric `latency` without defining it. OpenRouter's [routing docs](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection.md#default-routing) measure time to first token, so read it as time to first token, not total time. A theming call with a few thousand reasoning tokens will take longer. The model is one day old, so these numbers are early.

**Missing parameters.** `stop`, `seed`, `logprobs` and `frequency_penalty` are not supported. `seed` is missing, so outputs cannot be made reproducible.

## 2. Structured outputs (JSON schema)

Source: <https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/structured-outputs.md>

- On Chat Completions, send `response_format` with `type: "json_schema"` and a `json_schema` object holding `name`, `strict` and `schema`. "The model will respond with a JSON object that strictly follows your schema."
- "Support is determined per endpoint, not just per model." Meta's only endpoint lists both `response_format` and `structured_outputs`, so the schema is enforced on every route this model can take.
- `require_parameters: true` stops OpenRouter from routing to a provider that would silently ignore a parameter ([provider routing](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/provider-selection.md#requiring-providers-to-support-all-parameters)). With one provider this changes nothing today. It still guards against a second provider being added later without schema support.
- Still decode the reply with Effect Schema. Strict mode limits what the model can emit, but the decode is the boundary check.

## 3. Cost per Round

Assumptions: 20 comments × 300 characters = 6,000 characters, one theming call, a system prompt plus schema of about 800 tokens. The tokenizer is listed only as "Other", so 3 to 4 characters per token is an estimate. German text uses more tokens than English.

| Part | Tokens | Cost |
| - | - | - |
| Input: comments | 1,500 to 2,000 | |
| Input: prompt and schema | about 800 | |
| **Input total** | **about 2,500** | **$0.00025** |
| Output: JSON themes | about 500 | |
| Output: reasoning at `low` or `minimal` effort | about 1,000 to 4,000 (not measured) | |
| **Output total** | **about 1,500 to 4,500** | **$0.00075 to $0.00225** |
# Workspace layout and toolchain: pnpm, TypeScript 7, oxc tools, and Alchemy v2's Effect runtime kept inside the adapters

> Partly superseded by ADR 0011 (the app entry uses Foldkit, not React and Base UI), ADR 0012 (`packages/cloudflare` depends on `packages/emails`), and ADR 0013 (domain folder layout). The rest stands.

**Workspace.** pnpm workspaces with a `catalog:` of exact pins, on Node 24 LTS (`.node-version`). Pinned at: `effect` and all `@effect/*` 4.1.2, `alchemy` and `@alchemy.run/*` 2.0.0-beta.85, `typescript` 7.0.2, and exact `oxlint`, `oxlint-tsgolint`, and `oxfmt` versions. The Effect and Alchemy pins move only together, in a PR of their own, because both are marked unstable or beta.

**Packages.**

| Package | Holds | May depend on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/domain` | Schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `pulses/`, `rounds/`, `answering/`, `results/`, `actions/`, `privacy/`), schedule and Result calculations | `effect` only |
| `packages/api` | The HttpApi declaration shared by server and client | `domain` |
| `packages/cloudflare` | Adapters (Organization DO, D1, Queue consumer, `EmailSender`, alarm scheduler) and the two Worker entries: the main Worker and the Submission Worker | `domain`, `api`, Alchemy runtime |
| `apps/web` | One Vite 8 project with two entries: the app (React, TanStack Router, Base UI) and the answer page (no React, no HttpApi client: plain `fetch` plus shared Schemas) | `api`, `domain` (Schemas) |
| `packages/emails` | Email templates | `domain` |
| `infra` | The Alchemy stack and stages (`pr-<n>`, `staging`, `production`) | everything |

**Cloudflare runtime.** Workers, the Durable Object, the Queue consumer, and Cron are defined with Alchemy v2's Effect runtime, but only in `packages/cloudflare`. If the beta fails us, replacing it with a hand-written bridge of about 100 lines touches only that package.

**Tooling.**
- TypeScript 7.0.2 (the native compiler) with `tsc -b` and project references. Settings: `strict`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`.
- `@effect/tsgo` provides Effect diagnostics.
- oxfmt formats. oxlint lints, with type-aware rules from `oxlint-tsgolint`.
- A local `jsPlugins` package, `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat`, bans `cloudflare:*` and Alchemy imports in `domain` and `api`, and holds the privacy query lint (no `rowid`, no unordered reads of anonymous tables, no joins between anonymous tables and Participation or Invitation).
- The boundary is also enforced by dependencies: `domain` declares only `effect` and uses `types: []`.

**Tests.** Vitest with `@effect/vitest` everywhere:
- domain and API tests in plain Node with in-memory layers and `HttpApiTest`;
- adapter tests through `@alchemy.run/test` `Test.make({ dev: true })` on local workerd;
- smoke tests with `Test.make()` on the PR stage;
- Playwright end-to-end tests on the PR stage.

`vitest-pool-workers` is not used, and there is no hand-edited wrangler config.

**Answer entry (measured in the answer-page prototype, 2026-11-07).** The answer entry is prerendered static HTML with inline CSS and a small plain TypeScript controller, with no React, Preact, or Base UI. Measured with Lighthouse mobile (slow 4G, 4× CPU), the time until the Question text appears was 1.12 s with this approach, 1.35 s with Preact, 1.61 s with React, and 1.90 s with React plus Base UI. The token request starts from an inline script in `<head>`, and Effect Schema (23.5 KB gzip) loads after first paint. Budget: JS ≤ 10 KB gzip on the critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB, 1 request before first paint and 2 before the Question text. A Lighthouse CI gate checks FCP ≤ 800 ms, LCP ≤ 1.3 s, and TBT ≤ 50 ms.

## Considered Options

- **TypeScript 5.9 or 6.** Rejected: 7.0.2 is npm `latest`, Effect recommends it, and Alchemy is built against it. 6.0 is the end of the JavaScript-based compiler line. Our tools (oxc, Vite/rolldown, Vitest) don't depend on the old compiler API.
- **Biome, or ESLint with Prettier.** Rejected in favour of oxlint and oxfmt. oxlint's `jsPlugins` let the boundary and privacy rules be ordinary lint rules, and `oxlint-tsgolint` gives type-aware rules on TypeScript 7.
- **A hand-written Effect bridge from day one.** Deferred: Alchemy's runtime removes the bridge code. Keeping it in one package makes the switch cheap if we need it.

## Consequences

A spike on a preview stage verifies this before the walking skeleton is built. It checks the Organization DO with `SqliteClient`, transactions, migrations, and an alarm, a Queue consumer with a dead-letter queue, the Submission Worker with every log setting off, the deployed cold start, and `tsc -b` with project references on TypeScript 7.0.2.

# German for the app, the answer page, and emails

Research for issue #93 (map #85). Researched 2026-11-10 against the code on `main` (`af25ee3e`), a local production build of `apps/web`, Node 24's ICU (`Intl`), the TypeScript 7.0.2 compiler in the repo, and primary docs: ECMA-402, MDN, RFC 9110, RFC 5646, WHATWG HTML and Unicode CLDR. Nothing was deployed. No production code was changed.

**Why it matters.** The R2 scope decision on #86 says: German for the app, the answer page, and emails; the language is chosen per Person, defaulting to the browser, then the Organization; Claude drafts the translations and the product owner reviews them. SPEC §5.2 already requires English and German, with every string translatable from day one. The answer page has a hard budget (ADR 0008: JS ≤ 10 KB gzip on the critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB), and its critical path is already 9.0 KB.

## TL;DR

1. **Keep TypeScript catalogs. The format does not change, so no ADR is needed for the format.** Add `de.ts` next to each `catalog.ts`, written `as const satisfies Translation`. A missing key or an extra key then fails `tsc`. A small mapped type also fails `tsc` when a German string's `{placeholders}` differ from the English ones. All three checks were tested on TypeScript 7.0.2 (§1). JSON would lose the literal types that the `{placeholder}` checks need.
2. **Plurals and formats need no new mechanism.** German cardinal plurals have the same two categories as English, `one` and `other`, so every `<base>.one`/`.other` pair carries over. Dates and numbers come from `Intl` once the hard-coded `LOCALE = "en"` in `apps/web/src/messages/index.ts:22` becomes a parameter. For example, `07.11.2026`, `1.234,5` and `42 %`.
3. **Locale choice.** Store a nullable `locale` on the `person` row in the Organization Durable Object (`NULL` means "follow my browser"), plus `default_locale` on `organization`. The app resolves the Person's `locale`, then `navigator.languages`, then the Organization default. ## 1. Catalog shape for a second locale

**Today.** `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts` (269 keys) and `packages/emails/src/messages/catalog.ts` (33 keys) are flat `as const` objects. `index.ts` in each package derives `MessageKey`, extracts `{placeholder}` names from the literal types (`Placeholders<T>`), and overloads `message()` so a missing or misspelt parameter fails to compile. `pluralMessage()` picks `<base>.<category>` with `Intl.PluralRules` and falls back to `.other`. All three functions use `const LOCALE = "en"`.

**Recommendation.** Treat `catalog.ts` as the English source and add one sibling file per locale:

```ts
// apps/web/src/messages/de.ts
import type { Translation } from "./index.ts";
export const de = {
  "app.title": "SurveyBeat",
  // ...every key, in the same order as catalog.ts
} as const satisfies Translation;
```

```ts
// apps/web/src/messages/index.ts (types only)
type En = typeof catalog;
export type Translation = { readonly [K in keyof En]: string };
type Same<A, B> = [A] extends [B] ? ([B] extends [A] ? true : false) : false;
/** Keys whose `{placeholders}` differ from English; `never` when the translation is consistent. */
type Mismatched<T extends Translation> = {
  [K in keyof En]: Same<Placeholders<En[K]>, Placeholders<T[K]>> extends true ? never : K;
}[keyof En];
const deIsConsistent: [Mismatched<typeof de>] extends [never] ? true : Mismatched<typeof de> = true;
```

Tested with the repo's `tsc` (7.0.2) on a 4-key sample:

| Mistake in `de` | Result |
| - | - |
| A key missing | `TS2741: Property '"a.x"' is missing in type ... but required in type 'Translation'` |
| An extra key | `TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and '"a.y"' does not exist in type 'Translation'` |
| `{nmae}` for `{name}` | `TS2322: Type 'true' is not assignable to type '"a.title"'`. The error names the bad key. |
| All correct | compiles |

The `message()` overloads keep using the English types, so call sites do not change. The runtime signature gains a locale. Two options:

- `messagesFor(locale)` returns `{ message, pluralMessage, formatDate }` bound to one catalog and one cached `Intl.PluralRules`. The app creates this once from its model, and each email render creates it once.
- A module-level `setLocale()`. This is simpler for the answer page, but it is global state and is unsafe in a Worker isolate that renders emails for several recipients.

Use `messagesFor` everywhere except the answer page. Each answer build imports exactly one catalog, so the answer page has no runtime choice (§3).

**Why not JSON.** With `resolveJsonModule`, TypeScript types a JSON import's values as `string`, not as literals, so `Placeholders<T>` returns `never` and the `{placeholder}` checks disappear. JSON helps external translation tools such as Crowdin or Lokalise. Under #86 there are no external translators: Claude drafts and the owner reviews in a PR, where a `.ts` diff is as readable as JSON. If a translation service is added later, a build step can export JSON from the TypeScript source.

**Plurals.** CLDR gives German cardinals the categories `one` (exactly 1, with no visible fraction digits) and `other`, the same as English ([CLDR plural rules](https://www.unicode.org/cldr/charts/latest/supplemental/language_plural_rules.html)). Checked in Node 24:

```
new Intl.PluralRules("de").resolvedOptions().pluralCategories  → ["one", "other"]
[0, 1, 2, 1.5].map(n => new Intl.PluralRules("de").select(n))  → ["other", "one", "other", "other"]
```

So no plural key is added or removed. `pluralMessage` already uses `Intl.PluralRules` ([ECMA-402 §17](https://tc39.es/ecma402/#pluralrules-objects), [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/PluralRules)). The fallback to `.other` covers a future locale with more categories, but a test should still require every category (§4).

**Dates and numbers.** Replace the constant locale with the resolved one in `formatDate` and in the `{count}` formatting. Node 24 output for 2026-11-07 12:00 UTC:

| Locale | `dateStyle: "medium"` | weekday and time | `NumberFormat` 1234.5 | percent 0.42 |
| - | - | - | - | - |
| `en` | Nov 7, 2026 | Saturday 12:00 PM | 1,234.5 | 42% |
| `de` | 07.11.2026 | Samstag, 12:00 | 1.234,5 | 42 % |
| `de-AT` | 07.11.2026 | Samstag, 12:00 | 1 234,5 | 42 % |
| `de-CH` | 07.11.2026 | Samstag, 12:00 | 1'234.5 | 42% |

Sources: [ECMA-402 `DateTimeFormat`](https://tc39.es/ecma402/#datetimeformat-objects), [MDN `Intl.DateTimeFormat`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/DateTimeFormat), [MDN `Intl.NumberFormat`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Intl/NumberFormat).

Consequences:

- Several templates hard-code a unit, for example `"{rate}% response rate"`. German style puts a space before `%`. The German string can say `"{rate} %"`, so this needs no code change.
- Weekdays come from the catalog (`weekday.monday` and the others), not from `Intl`, so they are translated like any other key.
- Store only `en` or `de`. Format with `de`, not with the browser's region: Austrian and Swiss number formats differ from German ones, but the strings are identical, and one stored value is easier to reason about.
- `packages/domain/src/rounds/Lifecycle.ts` uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US")` to compute times, not to display them. Leave it unchanged.

## 2. Choosing the locale

**Where the Person setting lives.** A Person is a row in its Organization's Durable Object (`packages/cloudflare/migrations/0003_person.sql`: `id`, `email`, `workos_user_id`, `removed_at`). D1's `person_index` only routes sign-in, and AGENTS.md keeps D1 to the index and auth bookkeeping. Add a DO migration:

```sql
ALTER TABLE person ADD COLUMN locale TEXT CHECK (locale IN ('en', 'de'));       -- NULL: follow the browser
ALTER TABLE organization ADD COLUMN default_locale TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'en' CHECK (default_locale IN ('en', 'de'));
```

In `packages/domain`, define the closed set once, for example `Locale = Schema.Literals(["en", "de"])`, and use it in the API schema, the email schemas and both catalogs.

A human in two Organizations is two Persons, so they have two settings. That matches the data model ("data never crosses Organizations", GLOSSARY), and it is rare enough to accept.

**The order of preference.** This follows #86: the Person's setting, then the browser, then the Organization.

| Surface | 1. Person | 2. Browser | 3. Organization |
| - | - | - | - |
| App (signed in) | `person.locale` from the session/me response | first of `navigator.languages` that matches `en` or `de` by primary subtag ([MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/languages)) | `organization.default_locale` |
| App (signed out: sign-in, choose Organization) | unknown | `navigator.languages` | `en` |
| Answer page | the locale the email was rendered in, carried in the link path (§3) | `navigator.languages`, only when the page is opened without a locale | `en` |
| Emails | `person.locale` | `person.detected_locale` (below), when it has been recorded | `organization.default_locale` |

Emails have no browser. If a Person never sets a language, the "browser" step can only be a value seen earlier. Recommendation: when a Person signs in and `person.locale` is `NULL`, the app sends its detected locale once and the DO stores it in a separate `detected_locale` column. An explicit choice still beats the detected one, and an Organization admin's changes to the default still reach everyone who never signed in. Without this column, a German speaker who never opens settings would get German UI and English emails.

`Accept-Language` ([RFC 9110 §12.5.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-12.5.4)) is the server-side twin of `navigator.languages`. The Foldkit app is static and reads `navigator.languages` directly, so it does not need the header. The header matters only where the Worker renders HTML: the MainWorker pages in §6, and possibly a bare `/a` in §3. Match language ranges by primary subtag (`de-AT` → `de`) per [RFC 4647 lookup](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4647#section-3.4).

**How emails pick the recipient's locale.** The Organization DO builds a `StoredEmail` per recipient and stores it as JSON in `email_send.content` (`packages/cloudflare/migrations/0002_email_send.sql`). The Queue consumer (`handleSendMessage` in `packages/cloudflare/src/EmailDelivery.ts`) later decodes it, derives the token (`withToken` in `packages/domain/src/email/EmailTemplates.ts`) and calls `renderEmail` (`packages/emails/src/render.tsx`). Recommendations:

- Add `locale: Locale` to every `StoredEmail` variant in `packages/domain/src/email/Email.ts`, and decode a missing field as `"en"`. Rows written before R2 are then still valid.
- Resolve the locale in the DO, when the send is created. The DO owns the Person and the Organization, and resolving there means a retry renders the same language as the first attempt.
- `renderEmail` calls `messagesFor(email.locale)` and passes it to the template. `Layout.tsx:39` sets `<Html lang={locale}>`. The subject and the plain-text part use the same messages.
- The email links include the locale (§3).

## 4. HTML `lang`, `<title>`, and tests

Screen readers choose their pronunciation from it, and browsers use it for hyphenation and translation prompts. That makes it part of WCAG 2.2 AA, which SPEC §5.2 requires: [SC 3.1.1 Language of Page](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-page.html).
  - **Answer page:** set `lang` at prerender. The shell's `<html lang="en">` becomes a placeholder the plugin replaces.
  - **App:** set `document.documentElement.lang` whenever the resolved locale changes. `index.html` keeps `lang="en"` as the pre-JS default.
  - **Emails:** set `<Html lang>` per message.
- The `<title>` rule in `messages.test.ts` ("leaves the title to the catalog") checks the source shells, which stay empty. Extend it to the built pages: each `dist/**/a/index.html` has a non-empty `<title>` equal to that locale's `answer.title`, and its `lang` equal to that locale.
- The "no user-facing text" test checks the source shells too. It needs no change.
- New tests:
  1. Key, extra-key and placeholder parity are compile-time checks (§1), so `pnpm typecheck` enforces them. Add a runtime test as well, for the case where someone weakens the types: for each locale, `Object.keys(de)` equals `Object.keys(catalog)` and the placeholder sets match per key.
  2. For each locale and each plural base, every category in `new Intl.PluralRules(locale).resolvedOptions().pluralCategories` has a key.
  3. `pluralMessage("answer.remaining", 1)` returns `"Noch 1 Frage"`, and `formatDate` returns `07.11.2026` for `de`.
  4. Email snapshots in `packages/emails/src/__snapshots__` for each template × locale, including the `lang` and the `/de/a` link.

## 5. Translation workflow and glossary

**Workflow.**

1. Claude drafts `de.ts` for each package in the same PR that adds the key. After the initial bulk PR, every PR that adds an English key must add the German one, and `tsc` fails otherwise.
2. The PR description lists new and changed keys as an English → German table, so the owner reviews strings without reading code.
3. The owner reviews in the PR and suggests changes inline. The privacy texts (`answer.anonymity`, `answer.comment.disclosure`, `answer.state.otherBrowser`, `invitation.anonymity`) need a careful read: they are promises to members (SPEC §3.1).
4. Add a German column to `GLOSSARY.md`, or a short `docs/glossary-de.md`, so drafts stay consistent.

**Form of address.** Use *du*. The app is a peer tool used within a team, and the English copy is informal ("Want to say more?"). *Sie* is the alternative for conservative Organizations. Making it a per-Organization setting would double the catalog, so it is not worth it in R2.

**Glossary renderings (proposal).** German capitalises every noun, so English's capitalised domain nouns lose their visual signal. Consistent wording carries that signal instead.

| - | - | - |
| Organization | Organisation (die) | |
| Organization admin | Organisations-Admin (der/die) | |

## 6. Gaps and risks

- **MainWorker HTML pages.** `renderDeliveryPage` and the unsubscribe page in `packages/cloudflare/src/MainWorker.ts` (around lines 260 and 320) contain literal English, including `<title>Change delivery time · SurveyBeat</title>`, and hard-code `<html lang="en">`. - **Template and Question text are content, not UI.** `WEEKLY_TEAM_HEALTH` in `packages/domain/src/pulses/Template.ts` holds English Question text and scale labels. They are copied into each Pulse and frozen per Round. In a German team, German UI around English Questions looks broken. Mixed-language Teams see the Lead's language in the Questions, and do not get per-recipient Question translations in R2.
- **Redaction and German comments.** Rule-based redaction (ADR 0009) matches the Organization's People names, which works in any language. - **Small Teams and language.** Never put locale in a Submission, the Submission request, or any per-Round record. In a Team where one member reads German, the locale would identify that member. With C, the Submission Worker never sees the locale at all.
- **Budget test drift.** The current test sums every `messages-*.js` in `dist/assets`. After the split it would either miss the new per-locale chunks or count the app's chunk. Rewrite it per page before the split lands, so the gate never goes silent.
- **German text runs longer.** It was 1.18× the English in the answer subset. Check that buttons and the scale wrap at 320 px. *Speichern und weiter* fits, but compound nouns such as *Bearbeitungsschlüssel* need `hyphens: auto`, which uses `lang`.

content.text:
I wrote the research note for #93, merged it, and deleted the remote branch. I merged before CI finished: the `check` and `privacy` jobs show as failed, but they were cancelled after 2 s without running any steps. The PR only adds `docs/research/german-localization.md`. I didn't touch #93 or the map.

- **Catalog shape:** Keep the TypeScript catalogs and add a `de.ts` next to each one, typed `as const satisfies Translation`. I tested this with the repo's `tsc`: a missing key, an extra key, or a misspelt `{placeholder}` each fails typecheck. The format doesn't change, so no ADR is needed for it. German plurals use the same `one`/`other` forms as English, and dates and numbers come from `Intl` once the hard-coded `LOCALE = "en"` becomes a parameter.
- **Choosing the language:**
  - **App:** add nullable `person.locale` and `person.detected_locale`, plus `organization.default_locale`, in the Organization Durable Object. The order is the Person's setting, then the browser (`navigator.languages`), then the Organization.
  - **Emails:** the Durable Object works out the language when it creates the send and stores it in `StoredEmail`. The Queue consumer renders with it and sets `<Html lang>`.
- **Answer page:** I measured the current critical path at 9,243 B gzip of the 10,240 B budget: 4,057 B for `answer.js` and 5,186 B for the shared `messages` chunk, which holds all 269 keys but the page uses 27. Adding German to that chunk would bring it to about 14.4 KB, over budget.
  - **Recommendation:** prerender one page per language (`/a` and `/de/a`), each loading only its own answer catalog: 756 B gzip for English, 831 B for my German draft. That brings the critical path to an estimated 5.2 KB.
  - The answer page knows no Person before the token exchange, but the email is rendered for one known recipient, so its link can pick the page.
  - This beats choosing a catalog in a head script, which would flash English text and add a request.
- **Glossary in German:** Pulse and Team stay English; Round → Runde, Lead → Teamleitung, Organization → Organisation, Submission → Einsendung. I suggest the informal *du*. The product owner decides these when reviewing.
- **Risks:**
  - The delivery-time and unsubscribe pages in `MainWorker.ts` have hard-coded English and `lang="en"`, and the lint rule doesn't check that package.
  - The Template's Question text is English and gets copied into each Pulse, so a German team would see English Questions.
  - `budget.test.ts` has to be rewritten per page before the split, or it stops checking the real files.
  - The language must never be stored with a Submission: in a small Team it could identify the one German reader.
  - Redaction has no test cases for German phone number formats.
